conclusions.statement: All NULL standard relations are also NULL raw relations; no equals-to-NULL or NULL-to-equals transitions occur. All inequalities agree.
All rows have standard_flag=1 and empty comment/text qualification fields. Raw and standard numeric strings agree exactly.
NULL-at-3 counts are 13 HLM, 2 rat hepatocyte and 0 human hepatocyte; NULL-at-150 counts are zero in all three.

The pattern is compatible with unqualified quantitative results, and gives no observed evidence that standardisation alone removed an equals sign. It does not establish uncensored measurement semantics.

Original deposition conventions, upstream qualifier loss and rounding/reporting-limit treatment of the 15 NULL-at-3 records cannot be distinguished from the available records. No original depositor ACTIVITY table or record-specific confirmation was acquired.

documentation.summary: ChEMBL 37 defines standard_flag=1 as curated/set standard columns and 0 as defaults from published data. Relation fields contain constraint symbols; raw relation/value/units describe the original dataset. Both relation columns are nullable. No NULL-to-equals convention is defined here.
Current deposition instructions require RELATION with a numeric VALUE; NA belongs in TEXT_VALUE. They do not establish the rules applied to this older deposition.
ChEMBL documents unit standardisation, potential rounding, validity flags and qualitative activity comments; these are general processes, not evidence that a particular row was changed.

null_policy: JSON null is displayed as NULL; absent keys are MISSING_FIELD; neither is converted to equals.
